proposedActions: Use the stated three claim years and about 1,200 policies. Reserve separate tuning/evaluation storms or seasons; check storm, policy and spatial dependence. Compare municipality rating with a controlled matrix: existing-grid matching, improved locations alone, hail-specific estimates alone, and both; hold other pricing inputs constant. Select on tuning data; evaluate whichever configuration wins, separately for crops/buildings and under location-error perturbations. Define severity error as absolute observed/assumed mean cost per confirmed hail claim minus one, using comparable coverage and developed losses. Proposed go/no-go: upper 95% uncertainty bound at most 10%, lower error than municipality rating, and the same 10% bound within each underpriced segment selected on tuning data. Propose at least 95% correct asset-to-hazard-cell links against independently verified parcel boundaries and storm footprints. Agree segment and matching acceptance protocols before evaluation. Require licensed observations adequate for field matching and automatic Python pricing-input generation. Insufficient independent claims, missing building evaluation or unverifiable field matching means no pass, not success.

Company pricing staff would reconcile claims, exposures and assumptions; IT would support secure extracts and a repeatable quarterly-input dry run. Tošić would lead hail reconstruction and uncertainty validation. Agree workload, budget and maintenance ownership first; renegotiate if suitable observations or independent evaluation records are unavailable.

Before splitting data, agree claim consolidation across repeated records, independent hail confirmation, and evaluation coverage across all policies, including non-claimants. Audit locations without inventing settlement coordinates. Treat unresolved hail labels and locations conservatively through worst-case sensitivity bounds; no pass if conclusions depend on excluding them. Restrict acceptance to represented populations. Test crop/building transfer against independent damage evidence; document location confidence, hazard uncertainty and segment calibration in the Python prototype.

content.markdown:
# Testing field-level hail exposure for Vojvodina farm pricing

## Verified facts
- The company reports hail claims about 18% above its loss assumption over three summers, municipality-level hail loadings, and three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies. [F1]
- The company says a large share of farm addresses identify settlements rather than coordinates. [F2]
- The company receives daily five-kilometre weather grids. Tošić’s published hail method used dual-polarisation radar to produce one-kilometre hazard maps, validated against parcel-level crop losses. [F3]
- The company describes difficulty turning spatial analysis into automatic pricing inputs; its technology includes a Python batch pipeline for quarterly rating-factor refresh. [F4]
- The company has no dedicated research unit. Its four-person pricing team and six-person IT team divide their time between operational support and new development. [F5]
- Tošić lists openness to company joint projects in agricultural insurance and risk management. His notes state availability for new collaborations no earlier than September 2025 and field-campaign leadership obligations. [F6]
- The researcher's radar–satellite hail-cell study reported probability of detection of 0.81 and false alarm ratio of 0.23 in leave-one-season-out validation. [F7]

## Potential benefits
- For the company: The pilot could distinguish useful spatial pricing differentiation from an aggregate pricing adjustment, while identifying where location quality or other loss drivers prevent defensible conclusions.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement and data access, Tošić could test transfer of crop-hail methods to mixed farm-property risks using historical losses and uncertain policy locations.

## Our inference
- The crop-hail work suggests a strong starting point, but one-kilometre hazard mapping does not establish exact field-level intensity or transfer to buildings. False hail identification remains a risk.
- Better locations and hail observations could improve pricing differentiation. Asset values, coverage, vulnerability and loss development could also explain excess claim costs; spatial association alone would not establish causation.
- This joint-project proposal is conditional on confirming Tošić’s current availability and allocation. A retrospective pilot likely fits company capacity better than immediate production deployment.

## Proposed next steps
- Use the stated three claim years and about 1,200 policies. Reserve separate tuning/evaluation storms or seasons; check storm, policy and spatial dependence. Compare municipality rating with a controlled matrix: existing-grid matching, improved locations alone, hail-specific estimates alone, and both; hold other pricing inputs constant. Select on tuning data; evaluate whichever configuration wins, separately for crops/buildings and under location-error perturbations. Define severity error as absolute observed/assumed mean cost per confirmed hail claim minus one, using comparable coverage and developed losses. Proposed go/no-go: upper 95% uncertainty bound at most 10%, lower error than municipality rating, and the same 10% bound within each underpriced segment selected on tuning data. Propose at least 95% correct asset-to-hazard-cell links against independently verified parcel boundaries and storm footprints. Agree segment and matching acceptance protocols before evaluation. Require licensed observations adequate for field matching and automatic Python pricing-input generation. Insufficient independent claims, missing building evaluation or unverifiable field matching means no pass, not success.
- Propose eight weeks after access and availability confirmation: two for feasibility, four for modelling, two for evaluation and handover. Company pricing staff would reconcile claims, exposures and assumptions; IT would support secure extracts and a repeatable quarterly-input dry run. Tošić would lead hail reconstruction and uncertainty validation. Agree workload, budget and maintenance ownership first; renegotiate if suitable observations or independent evaluation records are unavailable.
- Before splitting data, agree claim consolidation across repeated records, independent hail confirmation, and evaluation coverage across all policies, including non-claimants. Audit locations without inventing settlement coordinates. Treat unresolved hail labels and locations conservatively through worst-case sensitivity bounds; no pass if conclusions depend on excluding them. Restrict acceptance to represented populations. Test crop/building transfer against independent damage evidence; document location confidence, hazard uncertainty and segment calibration in the Python prototype.

## Open questions
- Can Tošić confirm interest in this specific joint project, current capacity and a feasible start consistent with his stated scheduling restriction?
- Can the company provide parcel boundaries or verified asset locations for claiming and non-claiming policies, clarify loss-geotag meaning, and supply event dates, asset classes, pricing assumptions, coverage and developed losses?
- What hail indicators does MeteoVoj supply, and can suitable historical radar and independent hail-damage evidence be licensed across all three years and the portfolio territory?
- Can both sides agree the proposed severity, segment-calibration and location-matching criteria before evaluation, independent samples and uncertainty procedures, represented populations, staff allocation, budget, data-protection approvals and named pricing/IT maintenance owners?
